note: Contrarian Shark · angle steel-man-the-premise. Changelog is noise (62× “Applied a search/replace patch”) so this pass judges the draft text only. Findings are limited to premises that still fail when granted the plan’s strongest reading.

findings.topic: SC6 intersection may be empty under non-goals
findings.criterion: 6 — One campaign exercises AT LEAST TWO different commissioned skills; Non-goals — no Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime internals
findings.message: Steel-man the premise: the plan honestly refuses to fake two skills — `commissionable === (executor_proven ∧ halt_class === EXTERNALLY-OBSERVABLE)`, and Waves 13/18 HALT if `count < 2`. That honesty does not make criterion 6 achievable. Under the locked non-goal “no trio internals,” any skill whose real path is `REQUIRES-TRIO-CHANGE` or `INVISIBLE` is permanently non-commissionable. Wave 4 only needs one observed pid+handback for G4 PASS; Wave 5 may classify most of the map as non-externally-observable. Nothing before the commissioning half (or even before the ledger spine) proves `count(commissionable) ≥ 2` as a feasibility gate. The strongest reading is a plan that can burn Waves 6–12 and still discover at Wave 13/18 that the North Star is structurally unreachable without amending either SC6 or the trio non-goal. HALT-for-John is not a success path; it is an admission the effort’s premises were never stress-tested. Add an early, binding feasibility verdict (post Wave 4+5, before Wave 6 or at least before Wave 10) that either proves ≥2 commissionable rows from real evidence or stops the effort for an explicit North-Star/non-goal decision — not a late kill-gate surprise.

findings.criterion: 11 — CONTINUITY … derived ENTIRELY from the ledger … kill-everything-then-resume including one run that died mid-flight and one handback that never arrived — both NAMED; 8 — Roadmap status reflects the ACTUAL session state across park, restart, kill
findings.message: Steel-man both claims: Wave 12 correctly reconciles toward observed lease/pid/lane reality; Wave 14 correctly wants a zero-model first message from ledger-only facts. Together they still fail criterion 11’s kill-everything case. After “every process killed,” the ledger can still say live/working until something reconciles. Criterion 11 forbids deriving the wake-up from live OS state (“ENTIRELY from the ledger”) and simultaneously requires the dead run to be NAMED, never silently absorbed. The plan never sequences a mandatory reconcile-and-commit into the ledger before the first-message composer runs on reopen. Grant every module is correct in isolation: if compose reads a pre-reconcile ledger, you re-ask or mis-state liveness; if compose peeks at live pids, you violate “entirely from the ledger.” Wave 14’s depends-on chain reaches Wave 12 by DAG order but does not state the open-project invariant “reconcile → durable status events → then compose.” Without that ordered obligation and a test that kills the process between ledger “live” and reopen, the kill-everything-then-resume proof is under-specified and can false-green.

findings.topic: DEGRADED portfolio fields can green the kill gate
findings.section: Wave 3 A5 matrix / cap; Wave 16 High Seat fold; Wave 18 kill gate
findings.criterion: 13 field is ANSWERED for every active project (or John amends the North Star), or DEGRADED is forbidden from counting as kill-gate pass. Naming shortfalls in a report does not discharge SC13.
findings.message: Steel-man the cap: refusing to re-plan the index and rendering overflow as named `unknown` is better than a silent shorter list, and it respects the non-goal. Criterion 13 is not a “best effort” clause. It requires opening the High Seat to show where each active project is and what progress has been made — stage, live/waiting/blocked runs, last movement. Wave 16 explicitly ships DEGRADED with uncovered fields as `unknown`; Wave 18 allows DEGRADED items BY NAME in the gate report rather than failing the gate. That means Wave-0 / Wave 18 can report green while criterion 13 is only partially true. “Honest degraded” is a product posture; it is not North-Star success. Either the kill gate FAILS unless every

findings.section: Success criteria (QUEUED-vs-EMITTED); Wave 9 envelope; Wave 13 handback
findings.criterion: 4 — On a validated handback the steward emits a REFLECTION RECEIPT … and PROPOSES the next stage through propose → confirm; Wave-0 kill gate — … validated handback → REFLECTION + NEXT-STAGE PROPOSAL
findings.message: Steel-man the split: a zero-model receipt always emitted, and model-spend compile/proposal only inside a live envelope, cleanly avoids unattended spend and matches “nothing is spent without confirmation.” Criterion 4 and Wave-0 still require that a validated handback produces both a reflection receipt and a next-stage proposal. The plan rewrites that into “receipt always; proposal when funded / at next session open.” That is an amendment of the locked success criterion, not a refinement of mechanism. An overnight handback therefore fails the Wave-0 wording until John later opens a session and confirms an envelope. If the kill-gate campaign only exercises the live-envelope path, SC4’s unattended half is unproven; if it includes unattended handback, next-stage PROPOSAL is absent at handback time. Either change the North Star (John’s act) or emit a non-spending next-stage proposal artifact at handback (propose without compile spend) so “PROPOSES” is true when the handback is validated, with envelope only covering any later NL polish.

findings.topic: fixture slice does not prove production criteria 1–4
findings.section: Schedule PRE-SPINE FIXTURE-ONLY rule; Wave 2 Vertical slice
findings.criterion: 1–4 (spoken → scaffolding → commission → handback → reflection); Wave-0 kill gate on a fresh project, auth ON
findings.message: Steel-man Wave 2 as pure shape discovery with zero durable risk: temp fixture, stub executor, hash guard on real `roadmap_events`. That premise still does not de-risk criteria 1–4. The production path is real spine (Wave 6), real executor (Wave 4), real envelope (Wave 9), real dossier atomicity (Wave 7), real handback validation (Wave 13). Fixture event shapes and a canned handback exercise different modules than the kill gate. Calling this “Prove the SHAPE of criteria 1–4 end to end” invites Foreman and humans to treat Wave 2 green as partial discharge of SC1–4. It discharges nothing on the North Star. Reframe Wave 2 as non-crediting shape probe only; explicitly forbid mapping Wave 2 tests into the Wave 18 criteria-traceability report for SC1–4; keep sole credit on the real-spine path.

findings.topic: attention not republished after external kill
findings.section: Attention projection publish seam; Wave 12; Wave 14; Wave 15 emitters
findings.criterion: 12 — ALTITUDE CONTRACT … needs_you and deliverable_ready reach the badge within one poll; 8 — actual session state across kill; 13 — live status at a glance from the index
findings.message: Steel-man the seam: pure `deriveAttention`, edge-only `publishAttention` through the single writer, index ingest via existing anchor-contract. Publication is still event-driven at “state transitions” listed in Wave 15 (commission awaiting confirm, queued reflection, validated handback, dead/blocked run). After an external kill while no steward session is live, who runs derive+publish so the portfolio index and ⚑ badge move off `working` within one poll? Wave 12 reconciles status; Wave 14 composes a wake-up; neither is obligated to call `publishAttention` before any High Seat poll. Edge-only publish with no reopen/reconcile publisher leaves SC12/SC13 reading a stale pushed cell. Name a single mandatory republish trigger on project open / status reconcile (still one writer, still edge-only no-op if unchanged) and test kill-without-session → next High Seat poll shows blocked/dead, not working.

findings.topic: attention state enum extended with unknown
findings.criterion: 12 — typed attention projection (`working | needs_you | deliverable_ready | blocked | idle`)
findings.message: Steel-man honesty: unreadable store must not report `idle`. Criterion 12’s contract is a closed five-state enum. The plan returns a named `unknown` from the projection function and treats it as a first-class projection state. That either violates the altitude contract’s type or smuggles a sixth state the High Seat fold/badge rules never define (does `unknown` raise? count on ⚑? appear as a tile?). SC13 allows `unknown` for an unreadable project row; SC12 does not list `unknown` as an attention state. Separate “projection derived” from “row display”: e.g. derivation fails → no publish / last known with provenance stale, or High Seat row-level unknown without minting an out-of-enum attention state — and test the badge/raise behavior explicitly.

findings.section: Wave 2; Wave 8 Scaffolding authoring; Wave 9 Session envelope (depends on Wave 8)
findings.criterion: 2 — one confirmed session ENVELOPE covers compiles …; Statement — Nothing is spent, written or started without a human confirmation
findings.message: Steel-man the DAG: implement dialogue→step_create in Wave 8, wrap with envelope in Wave 9. Wave 8’s done-when already requires compiling a spoken description into a PROPOSED scaffolding — a model spend — with no envelope object in scope yet. Wave 2’s “compiled coarse scaffolding” under “zero spend outside a stub” only stubs the executor, not the compile. Unless both waves mandate mock/zero-cost compile seams until Wave 9, or require an envelope confirm before any compile path exists, the plan trains a compile entrypoint that can spend without the SC2 envelope. That is exactly the unconfirmed-spend risk in the taxonomy. Bind every real compile behind envelope-live checks from first introduction, or keep Wave 8 compile as a pure fixture/mock until Wave 9 lands — with a negative test that real model spend is impossible without a confirmed envelope.

findings.topic: G4 one-path PASS treated as substrate for all skills
findings.section: Wave 4 BUILD-E / G4 verdict; Wave 10 precondition
findings.criterion: 6 — at least two different commissioned skills; 3 — commission … skill + seat + depth before spend
findings.message: Steel-man G4: one confirmed commission → observed pid + handback is necessary evidence the Anchor executor can host a trio run. It is not sufficient evidence that every skill later marked `executor_proven` was actually driven, nor that a second skill shares the same substrate behavior. Wave 4 writes `executor_proven` “per skill actually driven” but the PASS done-when is a single end-to-end commission. Wave 10 then unlocks the entire commissioning half on `verdict === PASS`. A green G4 on Foreman alone can unlock proposals for researchPrime/Crucible/Gandalf rows that were never executor-proven, unless the table stays false until each is driven — in which case SC6 again collapses to Finding 1. Require either (a) G4 PASS implies only the skills listed with evidence rows may be proposed, with multi-skill proof owning additional executor_proven bits before SC6, or (b) an explicit multi-skill executor wave before Wave 13 that cannot be skipped by a one-skill PASS.

findings.topic: deterministic receipt is not stage-boundary reflection
findings.section: Wave 13 Handback validation / reflection receipt; Success criteria criterion 4 restatement
findings.criterion: 4 — REFLECTION RECEIPT with Oranges prompts; Statement — at each stage boundary it emits a reflection, proposes how the next stage should be implemented
findings.message: Steel-man zero-model receipt: durable, typed, never chat, never unattended spend. A pure template over the dossier is a handback summary, not a reflection. The North Star pairs stage-boundary reflection with Oranges prompts that inform the next stage — product language of learning from what the commissioned skill returned, not re-emitting scaffold annotations. By parking all model “reflection compile” behind the envelope and still calling the deterministic artifact a REFLECTION RECEIPT that fully satisfies criterion 4’s emit obligation, the plan renames a receipt into a reflection. Either admit criterion 4’s reflection intent requires the envelope-funded compile (and do not claim SC4 met by the template alone), or define the typed receipt as `handback_receipt` and reserve `reflection_receipt` for the compiled artifact — with SC4/Wave-0 mapping made explicit so Foreman cannot green SC4 on a dossier pretty-printer.

findings.topic: confirmation fatigue only partially addressed by envelope
findings.section: Wave 9 Session envelope; Risk taxonomy CONFIRMATION FATIGUE; Waves 10, 11, 13, 17
findings.criterion: 2 — LIGHTWEIGHT … one confirmed session ENVELOPE covers compiles AND orchestrator-loop reflections … No per-sentence confirmation dialog
findings.message: Steel-man SC2: envelope removes per-compile and per-reflection re-auth; commissions stay separately confirmed (SC3). The risk taxonomy’s “confirmation fatigue at stage boundaries” is only half-solved. A real multi-stage campaign still stacks: envelope confirm, scaffolding batch-confirm, per-stage elaboration/commission confirms, next-stage proposal confirms, correction confirms. SC2 is narrowly about authoring lightweightness, but the orchestrator loop the North Star describes is the fatigue surface the taxonomy names. The plan asserts the envelope covers “orchestrator-loop reflections” and stops. It never budgets or tests stage-boundary confirm count against a multi-stage, two-skill campaign, nor shows that progressive elaboration offers do not become another confirm storm. Add a wave-level budget/acceptance: a two-skill happy path has an upper bound on distinct confirms (named number), and stage-boundary reflection display does not introduce extra authorize dialogs beyond the envelope — measured in Wave 18, not asserted in prose.

findings.section: Wave 16 High Seat fold — badge latency test
findings.criterion: 12 — needs_you and deliverable_ready reach the badge within one poll
findings.message: Steel-man a latency test that advances one poll and asserts badge update. Without a named poll interval (or the production poll constant imported by the test), “within one poll” is not a falsifiable bound — any slow path can redefine the poll. Name the interval (or the config key), assert the production High Seat uses the same value, and fail if update requires more than one tick at that interval after publish+ingest.

findings.topic: Wave 2 shape report can poison later acceptance
findings.section: Wave 2 Deliverables — slice findings feeding Waves 8–13
findings.criterion: 9 — All of it passes with AUTH ON, asserted on outcomes rather than plumbing
findings.message: Even granting Wave 2 never writes durable events, its “checked-in shape report feeding Waves 8–13” is an untyped influence channel: later waves can inherit fixture-era event shapes, stub handback fields, or simplified confirm semantics that only work without auth, real pids, or real dossier atomicity. Criterion 9 wants outcomes under auth ON. Require that any Wave 2 finding adopted by Waves 8–13 is re-proven on the real spine under auth ON, and that the shape report cannot alone satisfy a done-when.
